seen_animation: A line-drawn lobster seen from the front: a tall body outline with a horizontal crossline near the top, a left claw drawn as an open V hanging down to the left, and a grey small lobster doodle at the far left with a grey table edge below. In frames 1-2 the right claw is a horizontal V at the upper right, partly off the frame edge. In frames 3-4 it drops into a downward-pointing V at the lower right. In frame 5 it swings left toward the body as a zigzag. From frame 6 to frame 16 the right claw lies as a long horizontal curve in front of the lower body, joined to the body by two arm lines that cross the body outline, and it holds there with almost no change.
seen_film: A large dark lobster stands on a cloth-covered table facing the camera, with a small lobster at the left. In frames 1-2 its right claw is raised and extended to the upper right, partly out of frame. In frames 3-4 the claw swings down to the lower right, pincer turned toward the camera. In frame 5 the claw sweeps left across the front of the body. From frame 6 to 16 the big claw lies horizontally across the front of the lobster, below the head, and stays there with only small adjustments; the antennae hang down and the left claw and small lobster stay still.
named_subject: A lobster (front view) swinging its large right claw down and across in front of its body, with a small lobster beside it.
evidence: Event and timing match: e.png 1-5 claw raised at upper right (film 1-7 raised), e.png 6-10 claw dropped to a vertical V at lower right (film 8-11 claw down at lower right), e.png 11-15 claw folds left across the body (film 12-16 claw sweeps left), e.png 16-50 hold horizontal across body (film 17-50 hold). g.png shows one continuous arc from upper right down and around to the front of the body with no reversals. Weaknesses: e.png 5->6 the claw changes from a horizontal V to two near-vertical strokes in one frame, while the film claw at 5-6 barely moves and only drops at 7-8, so the drop starts early and pops. e.png 11->12 and 12->13 the claw is redrawn from a vertical V into a sideways zigzag rather than rotating the same V. e.png 14->15 the zigzag notch disappears and the claw becomes a single smooth curve plus a crossing arm line, a redraw rather than a rotation; from 15 to 50 the moved claw has no pincer notch at all, while the film claw keeps its two-finger pincer shape the whole time. In e.png 15-50 the arm lines are drawn straight through the body outline, so the claw reads as stacked lines over the body rather than lying in front of it.
primary_gap: The moving right claw does not stay the same V-shaped pincer while it turns: it is redrawn at e.png 6, 12 and 15 and ends as a notchless curve, so the swing reads as shape swaps rather than one claw rotating.
closes_when: Across e.png 5-16 the right claw keeps the same open-V pincer drawn the same way as the left claw and in c.png, rotating and translating a little each frame from upper right to horizontal in front of the body, with its drop starting near e.png 7 like the film and the notch still visible in the final hold.
protect: The overall timing (raised, drop, sweep left, long hold) that matches the film; the continuous arc path shown in g.png; the still left claw, body outline with crossline and the grey small lobster and table placed where the film has them; the sparse straight-segment line style of the doodle; the steady hold from e.png 16 to 50 with no jitter.
identity_gap: The body and left claw match c.png's oval body with crossline and open-V claws, but the moving right claw loses the V pincer construction from e.png 15 onward and becomes a long smooth curve with an arm line through the body, which the doodle never draws.
